title: Respiratory Rate Trend — Opioid Sedation
scenario: A 72-year-old postoperative client is receiving IV morphine via patient-controlled analgesia after hip surgery. The nurse reviews the respiratory monitoring flowsheet over the first several hours.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.stem: How should the nurse interpret the trend shown on the respiratory monitoring flowsheet?

options.text: The client is developing opioid-induced respiratory depression and increasing sedation
The findings are expected and require no additional action
The client's pain is worsening and the opioid dose is inadequate
The declining respiratory rate indicates improving oxygenation

questions.rationale: The falling respiratory rate, dropping SpO2, and rising sedation score together indicate progressive opioid-induced respiratory depression, a medical emergency requiring intervention.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.stem: Given the 01:00 findings, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Stop the patient-controlled analgesia opioid infusion
Attempt to arouse the client and stimulate deep breathing
Prepare to administer naloxone per protocol
Apply supplemental oxygen and monitor oxygen saturation
Increase the opioid dose to improve pain control
Document the findings and reassess in four hours

questions.rationale: A respiratory rate of 8, SpO2 of 88%, and a somnolent client signal dangerous opioid toxicity: stop the opioid, arouse and oxygenate the client, and be ready to reverse with naloxone. Increasing the dose or delaying reassessment would be harmful.
